feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
In transaction design, the approach of signing the actual weight is favored over signing an upper bound on the weight. The challenge with using an upper bound lies in the necessity to specify this limit somewhere within the transaction's data structure. However, there are no remaining inconspicuous locations available to discreetly include such information, making this option impractical.
By opting to sign the actual weight, the process becomes more straightforward since the total weight can be implicitly determined and does not require additional explicit notation within the transaction. This method, however, introduces a requirement for the signer to know the complete transaction weight before the act of signing occurs.
Additionally, the operation DEPTH 1SUB offers a shorter encoding compared to DEPTH 1 NUMNOTEQUAL, highlighting a preference for more concise script operations when possible.
